record.original_question: For plane triangulations with no vertices of degree 3, does the number of proper 4-colourings tend to infinity as the number of vertices tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2 The number of 4-colourings of a plane triangulation with no vertices of degree 3 goes to infinity as the number of vertices goes to infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A plane triangulation is a simple finite planar graph embedded in the sphere such that every face (including the outer face) is bounded by a triangle. A proper 4-colouring of a graph $G$ is a function $c:V(G)\to\{1,2,3,4\}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E(G)$. Let $P(G,4)$ denote the number of proper 4-colourings of $G$.

Consider the class $\mathcal{T}$ of plane triangulations in which no vertex has degree $3$. Prove or disprove the following: for every integer $M>0$ there exists $N=N(M)$ such that every triangulation $G\in\mathcal{T}$ with $|V(G)|\geq N$ satisfies $P(G,4)\geq M$. Equivalently, show that
$$\min\{P(G,4): G\in\mathcal{T},\ |V(G)|=n\}\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published proof or refutation of the conjecture that the number of proper 4-colourings of a plane triangulation with no degree-3 vertex tends to infinity with the number of vertices. The conjecture is related to Birkhoff–Lewis-type lower bounds on chromatic polynomials at 4, an area with much partial progress but no clearly identified resolution of this specific statement.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of four colour theorem results without mention of a resolution of the stated conjecture for triangulations of minimum degree at least 4.
status_evidence.claim: No public reference identifies this conjecture as resolved.
